triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Both MCE membership aggregations ranged over a bare `member_of_household` name that did not resolve to the imported federal state-plan relation and compiled as an unqualified implicit relation, so the 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii) household bars and the (ix) member exclusions/eligible-member test were not evaluated over the household's actual canonical member set.
triage.triage_notes: Read the diff, both pre- and post-fix module text, the federal `us/policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition.yaml` relation definition (data_relation member_of_household, arguments Person, Household — consistent with the new projection's current_slot: 1 / related_slot: 0 for a Household-entity aggregation), and the cited provision via resolve_provision (us/regulation/7/273/2 resolved fine; the new proof atom's excerpt 'No person shall be included as a member in any household which is otherwise categorically eligible if that person is:' is byte-verbatim in paragraph (j)(2)(ix), and (vii)(D) reads 'Any member of that household is ineligible...', so both gates must range over the real household member set). The commit body is empty; the PR body describes the whole encoding, not this defect. The decisive prose evidence is the PROGRESS.md hunk in this same commit (not one of the allowed quote_source values, so the commit subject is quoted instead): 'The first full program compile exposed that a bare imported relation name with a local predicate remained an unqualified implicit relation. Replaced that alias with a private, tautological derived relation whose executable source is the fully qualified federal state-plan relation; both MCE aggregations now range over this complete canonical projection.' Repair chain context: c0487985b originally encoded a CA-local `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` data_relation; 2a0771d02 ('fix: close CalFresh MCE membership fail-open') deleted it and substituted the bare federal name; this commit completes the binding. REVIEWER CAVEAT: this is a borderline item. The intended meaning was already correct in words — the defect is a cross-module relation-resolution/binding failure whose consequence is a wrong member set (the household-bar aggregation silently fails open and the eligible-member test fails closed on an unpopulated relation). A judge comparing only module text to the statute could not detect it without knowing RuleSpec's relation-resolution rules, so if the corpus is restricted to source-text-detectable defects, prune this one; it is not mechanical under the stated definition, because formulas changed and the member set the gates evaluate over changed. The commit touched nothing else in the module (no parameter, version, effective-date, or scope changes beyond the two count_where arguments) and only PROGRESS.md besides.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical plumbing and could not: the diff rewrites two executable formulas' aggregation domain and adds an executable `derived_relation` rule, so nothing in the mechanical carve-out (hashes, pins, metadata, excerpts) applies. The same commit's PROGRESS.md states the pre-fix state verbatim — "The first full program compile exposed that a bare imported relation name with a local predicate remained an unqualified implicit relation" — so before the fix the `count_where` in `calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies` and in `calfresh_mce_status_conferred` did not range over the canonical federal `member_of_household` projection, and the engine's `infer_slots` shows the bare name lowers into an auto-emitted relation with `slot_entities: Vec::new(), derivation: None`. The corpus text of 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(A)/(D) ("Any member of that household is disqualified…") and (ix) ("No person shall be included as a member in any household which is otherwise categorically eligible if that person is:") are member-scoped tests, so aggregating them over an unbound relation instead of the household's actual member set is a member-set/scope divergence, not a polarity flip (the mis-binding fails open on the exclusion gate and fails closed on the eligible-member gate). wrong_entity_or_scope, which the taxonomy defines to cover "household member set," is the right kind.
triage.verifier_notes:
Supporting evidence, verbatim from the same commit's PROGRESS.md hunk (not the module diff, so not used as the decisive quote): "The first full program compile exposed that a bare imported relation name with a local predicate remained an unqualified implicit relation. Replaced that alias with a private, tautological derived relation whose executable source is the fully qualified federal state-plan relation; both MCE aggregations now range over this complete canonical projection." The added rule binds `source_relation: us:policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition#relation.member_of_household` with `current_slot: 1 / related_slot: 0`, which matches the engine's fixed `infer_slots` convention (axiom-rules-engine src/formula.rs: "Preserve the established runtime convention: current entity in slot 1, related entity in slot 0"), so the slot orientation is unchanged and the only semantic change is which relation is aggregated. `us/policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition.yaml` declares `member_of_household` as a `kind: data_relation` over [Person, Household]; the engine docs note that repo-backed execution requests "reject bare output, input, and relation names" and key relation rows by durable id (`…#relation.member_of_household`), which is why the unqualified alias could not receive the canonical rows.

Two caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1. Provenance: bfadb95594 is an intra-PR repair commit inside PR #1176, the PR that first encodes this module (file history: c0487985b → a350ed6ba → 4ce32e959 → e4d561a24 → 2a0771d02 → bfadb95594, all pre-merge). The defective state never existed on main outside the PR branch. If the corpus is meant to capture defects in shipped encodings, this is a WIP repair round rather than a regression fix.
2. Near-duplicate with its parent: 2a0771d0 ("fix: close CalFresh MCE membership fail-open") changed the exact same two `count_where` lines, deleting a CA-local `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` data_relation that could diverge from the federal household. Parent and child are two passes at the same underlying member-set scope problem; scoring both as independent fidelity defects double-counts one issue, and the "fail-open/polarity" framing belongs to the parent, not to this commit.
3. Character of the bug: this is a DSL name-binding failure whose fidelity consequence is the aggregation domain. A stricter "encoded meaning vs. source text" reading could file it as a compile/binding defect rather than a misreading of the provision; under the supplied taxonomy (which lists "household member set" under wrong_entity_or_scope) it still lands as fidelity, but that is the main axis on which this could be argued down to unclear.
